title: How did you ship on IOS
author: Acidswtf
selftext:
Hey,

I own an Android and an Windows PC. I did develop a couple of games for the Android Playstore ( none of them had commercial sucess. Anyway all my friends and colleagues have an iphone.  And id like to ship them too IOS too. I know there is this 100 dollar fee but ive read ive to own at least 1 apple product for registration and for authentification and then ive to sign the code over a mac.

What is the cheapest way to get my apps on IOS without me spending way too much money on Apple Products i dont want nor need. Id be willing to buy a refurebed iphone 14 but thats about it.

Would love to hear your workflow with Android to IOS

comments.author: Dramatic-Mongoose-95
comments.body:
I've heard the cheapest option is used Mac Mini

I usually ship to both iOS and Android, I typically start on iOS and build on Capacitor, so I can build for Android as well

replies.author: Acidswtf
replies.body: Ty. But id need an iphone too for testing right?  Or how do you test on both devices?

replies.author: AboundApps
replies.body: They have virtual phones and iPads for you to test with, but ultimately having a physical iPhone/Pad will be best

replies.author: Dramatic-Mongoose-95
replies.body: You can test in the emulator, they run all devices, but some stuff doesn't work easy like any hardware like camera or haptics or tilting device

replies.author: Dramatic-Mongoose-95
replies.body: I have an iPhone, and I bought a man Android just to test on real device because my app needs a camera and screen recording.

comments.author: ImpressiveGooseHead
comments.body:
Yeah this is some apple bs that goes WAY back. You basically have to buy their recent hardware, and sign up for a pretty expensive developer program each year.

They lock Xcode out of older Mac hardware, so you’re stuck upgrading if you want to keep developing.

Just a way to squeeze you, I guess.

comments.author: Prestigious_Edge_472
comments.body:
Get an M1 or M2 used Mac Mini (Depending on the price you find) that's your best and cheapest investment.

 If you don't want to make the investment and have a friend/family member who owns a Mac, you can use theirs until you figure out whether you want to continue developing for iOS or not.  
You can go with VM/cloud, but you'll spend more than the price of a used mini in less than a year and you'll suffer 10x as much.

Ideally you want more than 8GB of RAM, while 8GB will work, it will feel like you're fighting with it more than compiling. (you don't need an iPhone, at least not initially, you can test on your friend's phones and emulators, but you do need a Mac to sign with xcode.

comments.author: Jarred-Smith
comments.body: You can use GitHub to compile it.
